finding: The reliability-aware ensemble did not outperform the strongest frozen conventional references in raw balanced accuracy.
supported_claim: The framework should not be presented as a universally more accurate classifier.

finding: Low-confidence signal windows had a 69.88% error rate compared with 7.75% for reliable windows.
supported_claim: The framework identified a substantially more error-prone subset under unseen operating conditions.

finding: Low-confidence windows represented 10.21% of predictions and contained 50.62% of all observed errors.
supported_claim: Reliability qualification concentrated approximately half of the observed errors inside a relatively small subset.

finding: Low-confidence recording files had a 75.0% error rate compared with 12.5% for reliable files.
supported_claim: The framework identified more error-prone independent recording files during strict cross-polarity transfer.

finding: Low-confidence files represented 20% of recording files and contained 60% of the observed file-level errors.
supported_claim: The reliability mechanism provided useful file-level error concentration despite the small number of independent files.

finding: Version 3 produced 84.75% warning recall with a 6.96% false-warning rate.
supported_claim: The development process exposed a tradeoff between warning sensitivity and false warnings.

finding: The framework warned for 2 of 3 events and produced 4 operational false-warning episodes.
supported_claim: Event-level evaluation remained necessary because window-level metrics alone did not describe operational warning behavior.

finding: Raw classification quality and reliability qualification represented different objectives.
supported_claim: A model can fail to achieve the highest accuracy while still provide useful information about when its outputs are less trustworthy.
